paper_title: EssayBench Evaluating Large Language Models in Multi-Genre Chinese   Essay Writing
caption: Dataset Statistics. Note that Open denotes Open-Ended sets, Cons. refers to Constrained sets.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the sample counts across four distinct essay genres — Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository — for two types of writing prompts: Open-Ended (labeled “Open”) and Constrained (labeled “Cons.”), as defined in the EssayBench dataset. The vertical axis, labeled “Sample Count,” ranges from 0 to 130 in increments of 20, representing the number of samples per category. The horizontal axis lists the four genres in a fixed, non-sorted order. For each genre, two adjacent bars display the counts: the light blue bar represents Open-Ended prompts, and the light pink bar represents Constrained prompts. In all four genres, the Constrained sets contain more samples than the Open-Ended sets: Argumentative has 79 (Open) and 122 (Cons.), Narrative has 80 (Open) and 87 (Cons.), Descriptive has 68 (Open) and 100 (Cons.), and Expository has 62 (Open) and 130 (Cons.). The Expository genre shows the largest absolute difference between the two prompt types, while the Narrative genre shows the smallest. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, color intensity, or additional annotations beyond the numerical labels atop each bar. The chart provides a clear comparative view of dataset composition by genre and prompt type without implying performance or quality.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the sample counts across four essay genres—Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository—categorized by two dataset types: Open (Open-Ended sets, shown in light blue) and Cons. (Constrained sets, shown in light pink), as defined in the caption from the paper “EssayBench: Evaluating Large Language Models in Multi-Genre Chinese Essay Writing.” The vertical axis, labeled “Sample Count,” ranges from 0 to 130 in increments of 20, while the horizontal axis lists the four genres in order. For each genre, two adjacent bars represent the respective sample counts: Argumentative has 79 (Open) and 122 (Cons.); Narrative has 80 (Open) and 87 (Cons.); Descriptive has 68 (Open) and 100 (Cons.); and Expository has 62 (Open) and 130 (Cons.). Across all genres, the Constrained sets consistently contain more samples than the Open sets, with the largest disparity observed in the Expository genre (130 vs. 62) and the smallest in Narrative (87 vs. 80). The chart visually emphasizes this pattern through the consistently taller pink bars for Constrained sets.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm stellt die Verteilung der Stichprobenanzahl (Sample Count) für vier Essay-Genres – Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive und Expository – dar, wobei jeweils zwei Datensatztypen verglichen werden: „Open“ (Open-Ended Sets, dargestellt durch hellblaue Balken) und „Cons.“ (Constrained Sets, dargestellt durch hellrosa Balken), wie in der Legende oben rechts angegeben. Die horizontale Achse listet die vier Genres in der Reihenfolge Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive und Expository, während die vertikale Achse die Sample Count von 0 bis 120 in Schritten von 20 skaliert. Für das Genre „Argumentative“ beträgt die Sample Count 79 für Open und 122 für Cons.; für „Narrative“ sind es 80 (Open) und 87 (Cons.); für „Descriptive“ 68 (Open) und 100 (Cons.); und für „Expository“ 62 (Open) und 130 (Cons.). In allen vier Genres übersteigt die Sample Count der Constrained Sets die der Open-Ended Sets, wobei der Unterschied bei „Expository“ am größten ist (130 vs. 62). Die Balken sind paarweise gruppiert, wobei der Open-Balken jeweils links und der Cons.-Balken rechts innerhalb jeder Genre-Gruppe positioniert ist, und alle Balkenwerte sind direkt über den jeweiligen Balken numerisch beschriftet.
